key_insight: Frequency-division multiplexing enables superconducting quantum gate operations to share control lines, with a proposed framework reducing line counts by one to two orders of magnitude.
engineering_relevance: Shared microwave control could ease wiring-density and cooling-power constraints in large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers.
method: Encode gate controls in polychromatic microwave pulses.
Use band-pass filters within a periodically extensible hybrid multiplexing framework.
Demonstrate parallel frequency-multiplexed CZ and XY(π/2) gates with 1:4 multiplexing.
evidence_signal: The 1:4 demonstration reports average errors of (6.4±0.2)×10⁻³ for parallel CZ gates and (10.6±0.2)×10⁻⁴ for parallel XY(π/2) gates, with no statistically significant multiplexing-induced degradation.
watch_item: The demonstrated 1:4 multiplexing does not establish performance at the proposed larger scale, where frequency allocation, filtering and crosstalk require validation.
paper_title: A Control Line Multiplexing Framework for Scalable Quantum Computing
